title: Natural column-cokernel identification for the tensor bicomplex of resolutions
statement: Let R be a commutative ring. For every pair of R-modules M,N and projective resolutions P of M and Q of N [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], put A=A(P,Q) [def-weil-pbc-tensor-bicomplex]. There is a family e_{M,N,P,Q}: A.flip.opcycles(0) ≅ P tensor_R N [def-weil-pbc-chain-complex-tensor-module]. The family is chosen simultaneously for all modules and resolutions. For modules M,N,M',N', resolutions P,Q,P',Q', maps f:M→M', g:N→N', and chain maps a:P→P', b:Q→Q' satisfying a_0 followed by the augmentation of P' equals the augmentation of P followed by f, and likewise b_0 with g, e_{M,N,P,Q} followed by a tensor g equals the induced column-cokernel map of A(a,b) followed by e_{M',N',P',Q'}.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M3 (lemma-tor-left-right), proof: tensor double complex, cokernel-complex computations and functoriality paragraph; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00M3

proof.text: Construct the column augmentation termwise as 1 tensor the augmentation of Q. Bifunctoriality gives a chain map and annihilates the incoming outer differential.

Descend this chain map through the column cokernel. Tensoring the exact cokernel cofork Q₁→Q₀→N with P_p preserves its cokernel by right exactness. Thus the descended map is an isomorphism: apply ChainComplex.isIso_descOpcycles_iff, HomologicalComplex.exact_of_degreewise_exact and epi_of_epi_f, with Q.exact₀.map_of_epi_of_preservesCokernel and the fact that tensorLeft is a left adjoint.

For augmentation-compatible a,b, precompose the naturality square with the column-cokernel projection. The p_descOpcycles and p_opcyclesMap identities reduce the square to tensor functoriality and b₀ followed by Q'.π₀=Q.π₀ followed by g. Cancel the cokernel projection (an epimorphism).

proof_origin.place: Tag 00M3, proof and functoriality paragraph, using projective resolutions (flatness and lifting suffice)
